stops.note: 'hole of stone', used for holed stones such as the Men-an-Tol in west Cornwall; one proposed source of 'dolmen'
used by Théophile-Malo de La Tour d'Auvergne, a Breton-born officer and antiquary, for megalithic 'stone tables', perhaps also thinking of Breton taol 'table' + men 'stone'
taken from French archaeology; Ireland's Poulnabrone dolmen in the Burren is over 5,000 years old

current_meaning: a prehistoric tomb of upright stones capped by a large flat stone
